template.name: The Growing Problem
template.storyMechanic: A tiny problem is ignored, then grows larger and larger through repeated escalation, until the hero pauses instead of continuing to react, and identifies the real, smaller problem underneath the now-overwhelming one.
sceneStructure: Tiny problem: a small, easy-to-dismiss problem appears.
Ignored: hero (driven by the false belief) ignores or reacts carelessly to it.
Grows 1: the problem grows larger as a direct consequence of being ignored.
Grows 2: it grows again, now visibly harder to ignore, feeding on the hero's reactions.
Overwhelming: the problem reaches its largest, most overwhelming size.
Pause: hero stops reacting entirely â€” the pause craft technique.
Real problem: underneath the now-huge problem, hero identifies the small, real, original issue.
Resolution: hero addresses the real (small) problem directly, and the overwhelming version dissolves.

repetitionPattern.phrase/source: a short description of the growing problem's size/shape, restated with the same sentence structure each time it grows
repetitionPattern.variationRule: each restatement must use the same sentence pattern with an intensified word/image (e.g. 'a small cloud' â†’ 'a big cloud' â†’ 'a cloud that filled the whole sky'), so the growth is felt rhythmically
repetitionPattern.finalVariation: at the pause beat, the growth pattern is explicitly broken â€” the next line does not describe the problem getting even bigger, it describes the hero stopping

template.escalationPattern: This IS the escalation template â€” the growing problem should visibly double or intensify at each stage, feeding specifically on being ignored/reacted-to rather than addressed.
template.turningPoint: The pause beat, placed at the problem's largest point â€” the hero must stop reacting entirely before the real, smaller problem can be seen.
template.resolutionPattern: Resolution requires showing that the real problem was small all along â€” the 'growth' was created by avoidance, not by the problem's true size.
template.symbolIntegrationPoint: Symbol appears at the tiny-problem stage, buried/obscured as the problem grows, and is rediscovered at the pause, guiding the hero to the real problem.
illustrationOpportunities: The tiny problem, visually small in the corner of the page
The problem growing, taking up increasing page space each time
The overwhelming version, filling the entire spread
The pause and real-problem reveal, back to a small, clear, contained image
template.pageRhythmGuidance: Let the illustrated 'size' of the problem physically grow across the page spreads (small to page-filling) so the escalation is felt visually, then cut sharply back to a small, calm image at the pause.

events.label: SETUP
events.action: After spending a long time gaming or watching videos, Kavi sits down to do something else but struggles to focus. Kavi wanted to concentrate on the next activity. Kavi's attention feels scattered and their mind feels tired. While wondering what to do, Kavi noticed a round smooth stone nearby. The old thought came quickly: "My attention controls me."

events.label: ATTEMPT_1
events.action: So Kavi tried to study exactly how it worked. Kavi tried to push through it, and the feeling was still there, just as big as before.

events.label: ATTEMPT_2
events.action: Along the way, Kavi noticed the round smooth stone again. Kavi tried again, a different way instead. Kavi tried to focus even harder, and the feeling had not gone anywhere at all.

events.label: TURNING_POINT
events.action: Kavi paused instead of forcing focus, and noticed what was actually pulling at their attention, realizing I can guide my attention back to what matters.

events.label: ATTEMPT_3
events.action: This time, Kavi took a step back and looked at it fresh — Kavi took one slow breath, then looked back at just the one thing in front of them, and this time it actually came into focus.

events.label: RESOLUTION
events.action: Kavi finished the thought all the way through — clearer, with the noise finally out of the way.
